headline.title: Port Ellery keeps its downtown bike lanes
headline.dek: After an 18-month pilot, council voted 7-4 to make the lanes permanent, despite mixed results for local businesses.

scenes.question: What did council decide?
scenes.why: The decision and what it commits the city to are the news; the tiles state them without a paragraph.

scenes.question: Are more people cycling?
scenes.why: Four counts of the same measure over time; the climb is the pilot's main result.

data.note: Before: the month before the pilot. Then: city counters.

scenes.question: What else changed on the street?
scenes.why: Two before-and-after numbers carry the safety gain and the cost to drivers.

numbers.label: Injury collisions during the 18-month pilot
numbers.context: down from 31 in the 18 months before

scenes.question: Did businesses gain or lose?
scenes.why: Three changes in the same unit, with one negative: a diverging bar chart shows the mixed result at once.

data.note: Compared with the same period before the pilot

scenes.question: Why keep the lanes?
scenes.why: The mayor's words tie the decision to the numbers shown above.

data.text: The numbers made the decision for us... Fewer people are getting hurt, and more people are coming downtown.
data.speaker: Dana Whitcombe
